Your journey begins right now. Before you can begin dismantling the old world, you need to establish a foothold in the new one and dig into the environment.



## What is <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/>?

<span id="ch1.intro1.2"/> (also known as **<span id="assignment.2.1"/>**) is a modern, open-source hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) platform built on <span id="assignment.2.2"/>. It runs directly on bare metal and gives the bank enterprise-grade **virtual machines** on a cloud-native foundation, <span id="ch1.intro2"/>:

- **<span id="assignment.2.3"/> + <span id="assignment.2.4"/>/<span id="assignment.2.5"/>**: enterprise virtualization as native <span id="assignment.2.2"/> workloads. Underneath sits the same battle-hardened **<span id="assignment.2.4"/>/<span id="assignment.2.5"/>** pair that has powered <span id="assignment.2.6"/> virtualization for decades, which is why the platform can run a huge variety of guest operating systems, <span id="ch1.intro3"/>
- **<span id="assignment.2.7"/> (<span id="assignment.2.8"/>)**: distributed, replicated block storage across every node, set up and ready out of the box. <span id="ch1.intro4"/>, **any <span id="assignment.2.9"/>-compatible storage driver plugs right in**, freedom of choice, never lock-in
- **<span id="assignment.2.10"/>**: VLANs and isolated overlay networks without touching a cable
- **One open-source bill**: no per-socket <span id="ch1.intro1.1"/> tax
- **<span id="assignment.2.11"/> that actually listens**: SUSE customers consistently rate **SUSE <span id="assignment.2.11"/>** among the best in the industry, and their feedback directly shapes where the products go next. Try asking a closed-source vendor for a seat at that table

Because the platform runs *on* <span id="assignment.2.2"/>, containerized workloads can run on the very same cluster. Keep the division of labor straight from day one: the <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/> UI manages **virtual machines**; managing containers (and managing whole fleets of clusters) is the job of <span id="assignment.2.12"/>, which you will meet in a moment.

<span id="ch1.intro5"/>

| The old world (per-socket licensing) | <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/> |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------|
| ISAware proprietary <span id="ch1.intro1.1"/> | <span id="assignment.2.3"/> + <span id="assignment.2.4"/> |
| Proprietary storage array |  SUSE storage, or any <span id="assignment.2.9"/> driver <span id="ch1.intro6"/> |
| Closed-source SDN | <span id="assignment.2.13"/> + <span id="assignment.2.14"/> |
| ISAware Command Throne | <span id="assignment.2.15"/> |

No vendor lock-in. No virtualization tax. No proprietary kernel. **One platform, one bill**, <span id="ch1.intro7"/>.



## 🎯 Your Quest Objectives

1. Log in and inspect the unified dashboard
2. Meet Rancher Prime, the command center!
3. Validate the distributed storage fabric
4. Test your administrative terminal access
